clue.text: Second charge not at all apt

parts.note: to second a proposal is to back it
a ward is someone in your charge

explanation.surface: A second fee being levied seems wholly inappropriate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' reads as a time unit or a second fee, but it is the verb meaning to support.
explanation.definitionFit: Backward, as in socially or mentally slow, describes someone far from quick or capable.

clue.text: Fish that hurt dog

parts.note: the shad is a herring-like fish
ow is the cry when something hurts

explanation.surface: A fish has injured a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dog' looks like the animal bitten, but it is the verb meaning to follow closely.
explanation.definitionFit: To dog or shadow someone is to tail them persistently, a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: Pioneer travelling through time runs into French city

indicators.note: the three pieces before it are put inside the city's name, so into signals insertion

parts.note: Aix (Aix-en-Provence) is a city in southern France
via means by way of, travelling through a place
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A time traveller explores a French city on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pioneer' fits as an early female aviator, the pioneers of flight.
explanation.definitionFit: An aviatrix is a woman flyer, many of whom were celebrated pioneers of early aviation.

clue.text: Antelope ultimately lacking energy's run through

indicators.note: the antelope's name loses its final letter, ultimately pointing to the end

parts.note: the impala is an African antelope
E is the physics symbol for energy; the 's reads as has

explanation.surface: An antelope that has run out of energy is speared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run through' looks like a jog across the savanna, but it means to pierce with a spike.
explanation.definitionFit: To impale is to pierce or run something through with a sharp point.

clue.text: Queen departs from East for N African capital

indicators.note: in an across clue, reading from the east means reading right to left, so the pieces turn round

parts.note: a rani is an Indian queen
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: A queen leaves the East for a capital city in North Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' suggests a city such as Tunis, but here it means money: RANID read from the East gives the currency.
explanation.definitionFit: The dinar is the currency, or money capital, of Algeria, Tunisia and Libya.

clue.text: Bad driver booked, carrying gunners among 50 people aboard

indicators.note: the driver holds the other pieces within, so carrying signals a container

parts.note: Toad of Toad Hall in The Wind in the Willows is a notoriously reckless motorist
RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners
in means booked, as a guest booked in
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A dangerous driver is charged, carrying soldiers among fifty passengers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' is just a link word here. Toad, the reckless motorist from The Wind in the Willows, is a crossword favourite for a bad driver.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainload is the whole body of passengers that a train carries at once.

clue.text: Wish joy to count, at large after release

indicators.note: letters freed from their order are reshuffled, so release signals an anagram

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nobleman, freed from prison, is wished well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at large' looks like part of the release story but supplies fodder letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To congratulate someone is to express pleasure at their good fortune, wishing them joy.

clue.text: Drink shunned by old city dissenters going into another state

indicators.note: the drink loses the letters of the city, which avoid it, so shunned signals removal

parts.note: a liqueur is a sweet alcoholic drink
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city
a faction is a dissenting group within a party

explanation.surface: Rebels in an ancient city refuse a drink as they move into another country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' looks like a country but is a physical state: a solid or gas becoming liquid. LIQUEUR minus UR leaves LIQUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquefaction is the process of a substance changing into the liquid state.

clue.text: Foodie's irrational remedy no Scots should return without

indicators.note: in the older sense of outside, the turned word surrounds the rest
the Scots word is to be read backwards, returning

parts.note: nae is Scots for no
pi is the best-known irrational number
a cure is a remedy

explanation.surface: A gourmet's strange cure ought to come back unaccompanied.
explanation.walkthrough: NAE turned gives EAN, which wraps PI and CURE. The 's of 'Foodie's' stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicurean is a person devoted to refined food and drink, a gourmet.

clue.text: Labour leader of country's moving to the right

indicators.note: the leading letter of the country is the one that is relocated
in an across entry, moving right sends that letter to the end

parts.note: Spain is the country

explanation.surface: The head of the nation's party is drifting rightward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' and 'moving to the right' suggest British politics, but labour is effort and the shift is S going from front to back of SPAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Pains, as in taking great pains, means careful effort or toil.

clue.text: Not much left that poet's penned

indicators.note: the poet writes it inside his name, so penned means enclosed

parts.note: Thomas Hardy was a poet as well as a novelist

explanation.surface: Little remains of what the poet wrote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned' looks like writing, but it means shut in a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardly means scarcely or only just, conveying a very small amount.

clue.text: Musician's wary, heading off, returning after short time

indicators.note: the turned piece comes after the short time in the answer

parts.note: mins is short for minutes

indicators.note: the shortened word is read backwards, returning
the word loses its first letter, its heading

parts.note: alert means wary and watchful

explanation.surface: A performer is cautious and turns back after a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: ALERT minus A is LERT, turned to TREL. The 's of 'Musician's' stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: A minstrel was a medieval travelling singer or musician.

clue.text: Duo finally put in charge before a game

indicators.note: the charge piece comes before the a in the answer
the picked letter is placed inside the charge word

parts.note: to pelt is to rush or charge along

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of duo

explanation.surface: A pair is finally placed in command ahead of a match.
explanation.walkthrough: PELOTA is the Basque ball game played against a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Pelota is a court sport of Basque origin, played with a ball against a wall.

clue.text: Tarry, retreating in line, resolved not to be taken in

indicators.note: the turned word sits inside the reworked letters
the letters of line are worked out anew, resolved into a fresh order
the word goes backwards, retreating

parts.note: to bide is to wait or tarry

explanation.surface: Delaying, falling back into line, determined not to be fooled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolved' rearranges the letters of 'line'; 'retreating' turns 'Tarry' backwards, and that sits after the first three of the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inedible cannot be eaten, so it is not to be swallowed.

clue.text: Drink? Bachelor ready for it

parts.note: randy means sexually eager, ready for it

explanation.surface: A drink? The single man is up for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready for it' is a coy phrase for being sexually keen.
explanation.definitionFit: Brandy is a spirit distilled from wine, a classic drink.

clue.text: Patron's first name omitted from material introduced into court

indicators.note: the shortened fabric goes inside the court abbreviation
the letter is dropped out of the fabric word

parts.note: linen is a fabric

indicators.note: the first letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for name; the first of the two N letters goes

explanation.surface: A sponsor's first name is left off fabric presented in court.
explanation.walkthrough: LINEN loses its first N, giving LIEN, inside CT. The 's of 'Patron's' stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: A patron of a shop or business is a customer, one who buys its services.

clue.text: In oasis when horse leaves, see small rodent

indicators.note: the see abbreviation goes in the shortened oasis word
the horse letter departs from the word, so leaves means removal

parts.note: an oasis is a waterhole in the desert
H is slang for heroin, which is also called horse
V is short for vide, Latin for see

explanation.surface: At an oasis, once the horse has gone, you spot a little rodent.
explanation.walkthrough: WATERHOLE minus H gives WATEROLE, with V put in.
explanation.definitionFit: The water vole is a small burrowing rodent living along riverbanks.

clue.text: A retired gent unexpectedly back in the corporation?

indicators.note: an unexpected arrangement of the letters is called for, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: A pensioned man surprisingly returns to the company.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as playful: someone rejoining the body corporate.
explanation.definitionFit: Being reintegrated means being restored as a part of a whole, such as a firm.

clue.text: Border chicken crossing the road?

indicators.note: the hen spans the road, so crossing means one goes across the other

parts.note: a hen is a chicken
the M1 is Britain's main motorway, written MI in crosswords

explanation.surface: The old joke of a chicken crossing the road, set at a border.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the joke 'Why did the chicken cross the road?'; here HEN crosses MI, Britain's M1 motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: To hem in is to surround or border something closely, confining it.

clue.text: State supporting women's clothing for male guide

indicators.note: in a down entry, the state sits below the clothing, holding it up

parts.note: drag is women's clothing worn by a man
Oman is a state in Arabia

explanation.surface: A country backs cross-dressing for a man who leads tours.
explanation.walkthrough: A dragoman was an interpreter and guide in the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragoman is an interpreter and guide in Arabic- or Turkish-speaking countries.

clue.text: Coaxed wife and daughter inclined to go outside

indicators.note: the inclined word goes around the daughter letter

parts.note: a ship that heels is inclined to one side

explanation.surface: A wife and daughter, keen to go out, used persuasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inclined to go outside' reads as wanting an outing, but the heeling word wraps D.
explanation.definitionFit: Wheedled means persuaded by flattery, sweetly coaxed.

clue.text: Concentrate, catching what the strained bill settler shows?

indicators.note: catching here means hearing, so the phrase is judged by its sound

parts.words: what the strained bill settler shows
parts.note: someone stressed by paying a bill shows payer tension

explanation.surface: Focus, noting the strain of someone paying up.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'payer tension' said out loud matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To concentrate is to fix one's mind closely, to heed carefully.

clue.text: Counterfeit pound secures present without query

indicators.note: the reworked letters hold the other piece fast inside
counterfeit means fake, so the letters are falsified into a new order

parts.note: to pose a problem is to present it

explanation.surface: A fake pound coin holds a gift without question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without query' looks like a stray phrase, but it is the definition: nobody has raised an objection. 'Counterfeit' shuffles the letters of 'pound'.
explanation.definitionFit: Unopposed means without objection or challenge, no one raising a query.

clue.text: Conservative fast food, thoroughly reliable

parts.note: blue is the colour of the British Conservative party
a chip is a fried potato, staple fast food

explanation.surface: A Tory eating fast food is dependable.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue-chip describes a sound, dependable investment or company.

clue.text: Landowner grabbing tail of rather large rodent

indicators.note: the landowner takes hold of the letter, putting it inside

parts.note: a squire is a country landowner

indicators.note: tail means the last letter of rather

parts.note: L is the clothing abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A country gent seizes the end of a fairly large rodent.
explanation.walkthrough: SQUIRE takes in R, then L follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The squirrel is a bushy-tailed tree-climbing rodent.

clue.text: Note winged creature crawling up part of leaf

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a bird is a winged creature

explanation.surface: Observe a bird inching along part of a leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: The midrib is the central vein running along a leaf.

clue.text: With king away, soldier's defiled Arthurian queen

indicators.note: defiled means spoiled, so the letters are corrupted into a new order
with the king away, his letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written, the 's being is
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: The soldier is disgraced once the king has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: SOLDIER without R is SOLDIE, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolde, wife of King Mark of Cornwall, is a queen in Arthurian legend.

clue.text: On both sides of line, squad's not yet fired

indicators.note: the squad word flanks the line letter on either side

parts.note: a unit is a squad

explanation.surface: A firing squad lined up has yet to shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fired' suggests shooting or sacking, but it means set alight.
explanation.definitionFit: Unlit means not yet lit, like a fire not yet set burning.
